description: Frozen real-Go observations of `symbrain memory sync` (pull, push, plain and encrypted relay, auth, URL validation, redirects, gzip, timeouts, malformed pages, tombstone conflicts). One JSON file per scenario: scripted fake-server responses, the HTTP requests the Go CLI sent (relay blobs decrypted: nonces are random), stdout, stderr, exit status and the database after the run.
worktree_commit_at_capture: 44d59150760769dc6d218eb736b93991cc65acef (+ uncommitted native Rust work; Go sources unchanged)
capture_env: env_clear + PATH=/usr/bin:/bin, HOME/XDG_*/TMPDIR under builds/symaira-brain/MEM-SYNC/work/go/<scenario>/, TZ=UTC, LC_ALL=C.UTF-8; scripted fake server on 127.0.0.1
replay: rust/symbrain-cli/tests/memory_sync_replay.rs runs the native binary against a Rust fake server with the same scripts; no Go needed
platform_specific: refuse/url scenarios that dial and fail print POSIX errno texts (darwin: `can't assign requested address`)
net_connection_refused_localhost depends on the host resolving localhost
accepted_differences: a bearer token with non-ASCII bytes: Go sends the bytes, the native HTTP stack refuses the header (error instead of a request)
https certificate-verification failures use the native TLS stack's wording, not Go's x509 texts; trust anchors are the bundled web PKI roots, not the system store
HTTP(S)_PROXY handling for non-loopback remotes follows the native HTTP stack's environment rules
normalizations: ports -> {PORT}/{CLOSED}, scratch root -> {root}, Go goroutine traces -> <trace>
database timestamps within a day of the run -> <now> (local-clock trigger stamps)
database REAL cells -> real:<IEEE-754 bits hex> (exact comparison; applied by capture.py, and once by script to the first 58 frozen files, whose floats were Python reprs of the sqlite values)
relay request bodies: each blob replaced by its decrypted payload (random salt/nonce)
